Twin Powerful Earthquakes Strike Panama, Triggering Evacuations and Regional Alerts

✍️ By Abhishek Pandey, WorldWire Desk  |  ⏱️ Published October 10, 2026 at 02:33 UTC  |  📰 Wire Attribution: Associated Press
Photojournalism wire visual • Attributed to Associated Press editorial archive
Executive Briefing: Central America was shaken Friday afternoon when a massive magnitude 7.7 earthquake and a subsequent 6.6 tremor struck southern Panama hours apart. The shallow quakes rattled high-rises in Panama City, caused structural damage near the epicenter, and prompted coastal alerts across the Pacific basin.

PANAMA CITY — A pair of powerful earthquakes struck Panama in rapid succession on Friday, sending shockwaves across Central America, collapsing structures near the epicenter, and forcing tens of thousands of residents into the streets. According to the U.S. Geological Survey, the primary tremor registered at magnitude 7.7 at a shallow depth of approximately 10 kilometers near Pitaloza Arriba in Herrera province, followed two and a half hours later by a second magnitude 6.6 quake near Río Grande. The violent shaking was felt as far away as neighboring Colombia and rattled skyscrapers across the capital, Panama City, more than 100 miles to the north, where terrified office workers fled high-rise buildings and falling debris damaged vehicles.

Emergency services reported significant localized damage, including the dramatic collapse of a historic 16th-century cathedral's bell tower in Penonomé and structural cracking in residential neighborhoods. Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino addressed the nation Friday evening, stating that civil defense teams had been mobilized across all central provinces to assess casualties and infrastructure resilience. Regional leaders quickly voiced solidarity, with Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella pledging immediate emergency assistance. Geological specialists noted that Panama sits atop the volatile intersection of the Cocos, Nazca, and Caribbean tectonic plates along the Pacific Ring of Fire, marking this the most intense seismic sequence to strike the nation since the devastating 1991 Bocas del Toro earthquake.

While oceanic tsunami monitors quickly downgraded initial Pacific-wide tidal wave warnings for Panama, Colombia, and Ecuador, civil protection authorities remain on maximum alert for persistent aftershocks. The Panama Canal Authority initiated comprehensive safety evaluations across locks, channels, and water reservoirs, reporting preliminary operations intact while technical teams inspect critical transit corridors. International aid agencies and local emergency responders are prioritizing remote communities in Herrera and Los Santos provinces as search-and-rescue teams work through damaged roads to evaluate the full extent of the disaster.
